mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or UNRATE decrease does not correlate with increased consumer spending within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST, or HOUST increase does not correlate with GDP growth within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a supply shock, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO decrease does not correlate with negative economic indicators within 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not correlate with negative economic indicators within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with increased consumer spending within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over 3 months signals robust consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances following a sustained increase in RSAFS, or RSAFS increase does not correlate with GDP growth within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) decreases by more than 0.5% in 3 months and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.5% in 3 months and UNRATE < 4%
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy in strong labor market
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of decreasing FEDFUNDS and low UNRATE does not correlate with positive economic indicators within 3 months.
